livingcolonists.configuration.baseUrl.to: Address of an OpenAI-compatible API, without /chat/completions. Examples: https://api.deepseek.com, https://openrouter.ai/api/v1, http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1 for a local Ollama. Default: https://api.deepseek.com.
Model for colonists' replies, for working out whom a message is for, and for colony chatter: the most used one, so fast and cheap is best. The exact name from the provider's model list (see Load models). Default: deepseek-flash.
livingcolonists.configuration.characterM: Model for rare, heavier work: writing colonists' backgrounds and writing conversations down into memory. Can be smarter and slower, for example deepseek-v4-pro. Empty: the chat model does it.
livingcolonists.configuration.apiKey.too: The provider's API key. Kept in the config file as plain text, so don't share the file. Leave empty to read the key from the environment variable below instead. Never sent to players.
Name of the environment variable that holds the API key; used when the key above is empty. Default: LIVINGCOLONISTS_API_KEY.
livingcolonists.configuration.timeoutSec: How long to wait for one answer before giving up and retrying, in seconds. From 1 to 300, default 30. Reasoning models may need 30 to 60.
livingcolonists.configuration.retries.to: How many times to retry after a temporary failure: a timeout, a rate limit (429), a server error (5xx) or a lost connection. Waits 1, 3, then 8 seconds. A wrong key or a bad request is not retried. From 0 to 5, default 3.
livingcolonists.configuration.useTools.t: On: colonists look things up and take orders through function calling (stock, buildings, research, jobs, crafting, couriers, guards and more); needs perception above off. Turn off if your provider doesn't support tools. Default on.
Upper limit of tokens for one answer. Reasoning models count their thinking here too, so keep it well above a chat line; the mod raises it by itself for heavy tasks. From 16 to 32768, default 2000.
livingcolonists.configuration.temperatur: How varied the answers are: 0 is predictable, 1 is natural, 2 is wild. From 0 to 2, default 1.
livingcolonists.configuration.extraParam: Extra fields added to every request, as a JSON object, for provider-specific options; {} for none. Example: {"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}} turns off DeepSeek's thinking for faster but less careful answers.
livingcolonists.configuration.fallbackEn: On: when the main API still fails after all retries, the request goes to a second API, for example a local model. Needs the fallback address and model. Default off.
livingcolonists.configuration.fallbackBa: Address of the fallback API, without /chat/completions. Example for Ollama: http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1.
livingcolonists.configuration.fallbackMo: Model of the fallback API, used for every kind of request. Example: qwen2.5:14b. Empty: no fallback.
livingcolonists.configuration.fallbackAp: Key of the fallback API, plain text. Empty for APIs that need none, such as a local model.
Environment variable with the fallback key, used when the key above is empty. Empty: none.
livingcolonists.configuration.embeddings: Address of the embeddings API, without /embeddings. Default: OpenRouter.
Embedding model, as the provider names it. It must know the players' languages: baai/bge-m3 does, and is cheap and fast. Empty: embeddings off.
Key of the embeddings API, plain text. Empty: the variable below. Without a key, embeddings are off, except for an API on this machine (localhost), which needs none.
Environment variable with the embeddings key, used when the key above is empty.
livingcolonists.configuration.profile.to: How deep colonists go, and how many tokens they spend. MINIMAL: the colony run by chat, plain answers, look-ups and orders, no character, memory or chatter, cheapest. LIGHT: a short character and memory. DEFAULT: the balance. IMMERSIVE: detailed knowledge, long memory, long colony chats, the most tokens. Personality, perception, memory and conversation can override parts of it. Default: DEFAULT.
livingcolonists.configuration.personalit: Colonists' archetypes and backgrounds. profile: as the profile says. off: none. low: the archetype only. default: the archetype and a short background. high: a longer background.
livingcolonists.configuration.perception: What colonists know about themselves and the colony. profile: as the profile says. off: nothing. low: their work and needs. default: also home, food, health, mood, weather, family, coworkers and colony look-ups. high: also siblings and more detail.
livingcolonists.configuration.memory.too: What colonists remember of talks, promises and gossip. profile: as the profile says. off: nothing. low: 4 lines of a talk and 5 facts, for about 2 days. default: 10 lines and 15 facts, about a week. high: 40 lines and 60 facts, about a month.
livingcolonists.configuration.conversati: How colony chats run on their own. profile: as the profile says. off: one answer to a player. low: up to 4 lines. default: up to 8. high: up to 16, colonists chat with each other a lot. Also turns colonists' own colony talk about events and their promise reminders on or off.
livingcolonists.configuration.cooldownSe: Shortest time between two messages of one player to colonists, in seconds; guards against spam. 0 turns it off. From 0 to 60, default 3.
livingcolonists.configuration.playerName: What colonists call players instead of their nicknames. One entry per player: Nickname=Name,Other name,Rare name; the first name is used most. Separate entries with ";", like Steve=Steven,Stevie; Alex=Alexandra,Alex. Empty: nicknames.
livingcolonists.configuration.colonyChat: On: colony members (owner, officers, friends) read their colony's chat and write to it from anywhere. Off: only players inside the colony's borders take part. Default off.
livingcolonists.configuration.membersOnl: On: only the colony's owner, officers and friends may talk to its colonists, and only the owner and officers may give orders. Off: any player inside the colony may. Default on.
livingcolonists.configuration.messagesPe: How many messages one player may send to colonists in an hour of server time; after that they wait. Against spam on public servers. 0: no limit (default).
livingcolonists.configuration.tokensPerD: How many tokens (prompt and answer together) the whole server may spend in a day; after that colonists rest until midnight. Counted since the server started. 0: no limit (default).

livingcolonists.configuration.initiative: How often colonists write to a player first, unprompted: about a problem of theirs (more pointed if it stays unsolved, until they give up asking), something the player told them, news or small talk. Any colonist, while the player is in the colony and not in a conversation, at uneven times. profile: as the profile says. off: never. low: about every half hour. default: about every 12 minutes. high: about every 6 minutes.
livingcolonists.configuration.speechBubb: On: colonists' lines also show as speech bubbles over their heads, and dots while they type, for players with the mod; the chat line stays. Private lines bubble only for their player. Default on.
livingcolonists.configuration.playerBubb: On: players get speech bubbles too, for their chat and colony chat lines, and dots while they type. Only players with the mod see bubbles. Default off.
livingcolonists.configuration.bubbleRang: How far away, in blocks, speech bubbles are seen. From 8 to 64, default 24.
